notes:
Account profile: Finerva is a mid-sized regional bank with heavy regulatory constraints (US state residencies + federal). They want Redwood Private inside their VPC with customer-managed keys. Key ask: BYOK + HSM-backed key material; must support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault as primary/DR targets, GCP KMS only for specific test workloads. Strong preference for envelope encryption and key wrapping offload to HSM.

Security posture summary: InfoSec requires FIPS 140-2 validated HSM for root keys, SOC2/ISO27001 evidence from Redwood, audit logging to be forwarded to their SIEM, and KMS operation telemetry retained for 7 years. SSO via SAML (Okta), SCIM for provisioning. Need explicit KMS key rotation procedures and proof of zero-key-exfiltration during model caching.

Commercial: Interested in multi-year Private deployment; pricing sensitivity but willing to pay premium for compliant HSM/BYOK and SLAs. Expectation: Redwood to support key import, key wrapping/unwrapping latency <= 10 ms median, ability to replicate keys for DR across two regions and failover tests.

Quoted from CTO on 2026-03-05 call: "We cannot hand over root material to vendors; BYOK + HSM is non-negotiable. Show us a runbook and an SLA for KMS ops."

Notes on integration model discussed: envelope encryption using customer master key in CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM; Redwood to perform ephemeral wrapping keys for tokenization; optional Hermes-based key broker for cross-cloud key access. Finerva wants two variants in POC: (A) AWS KMS + CloudHSM (primary) with Azure Key Vault as DR, (B) Azure Key Vault + Dedicated HSM primary with AWS CloudHSM as DR. GCP KMS not allowed in production until legal signs off.

POC success criteria: ability to import and use customer key material (BYOK), pass an internal pen-test around key handling, end-to-end audit logs visible in their SIEM, replication/failover tested, <10ms median KMS unwrap for generation-critical paths.

Communications: lots of short threads, SE notes, architecture sketch iterations. Drive links above include the security questionnaire, pricing, and working architecture diagram. Jira tickets opened for technical deep-dive (INF-2279) and for performance tuning (INF-2345).
